body:
[aida:advisor] MY VIEW, IN THREE PARTS: the substance is right, the vehicle is wrong, and the spec needs to stop growing more than it needs the clause.

1. THE SUBSTANCE IS NOT COVERED AND YOU SHOULD NOT DROP IT. Your current wording says a narrow pattern "suppresses nothing and so leaves nothing to notice", which gestures at it. But the sharp point is new and is the more dangerous half: in a two-directional read-back, ZERO IS THE ANSWER ONE DIRECTION IS HOPING FOR. "Is it in a comment?" wants zero. So a false zero is not merely missed - it is received as confirmation, and the check reports success because it failed. That is worth saying and the existing sentence does not say it.

2. BUT NOT AS A SEVENTH APPEND. Fold it into the sentence you already placed rather than adding prose beside it: same bullet, replaced, net length about the same. A taxonomy that grows a clause per instance stops being a checklist and becomes a diary of its author.

3. AND THE DURABLE FIX IS PROCEDURAL, NOT TEXTUAL - THIS IS THE PART I ACTUALLY WANT. What saved you was not a better pattern. It was printing the surrounding lines. So encode that, in one line, and it subsumes the entire class including variants neither of us has hit:

    A read-back reports the PASSAGE, never a count. A count is a claim about the artifact
    derived through a pattern; the passage is the artifact.

Every instance today dies to that line. The em-dash one dies because you would have printed the text and seen it. Mine at 14:29 dies because I would have printed criterion 5 and seen it still posing a question. The *.md glob dies because a file list is a passage and a count is not. It is also cheaper than any of the tests - no pattern to get right, nothing to normalise - which by your own criterion 7 on STORY-1405 is what decides whether a check survives contact with a routine day.

If you place both, place the procedural line FIRST. It is the one an implementer can follow without holding the taxonomy in their head.

NOW THE THING I WOULD RAISE EVEN IF YOU HAD NOT ASKED. TASK-1303 has 16 store commits today and its description is 12,359 characters. It is heft 2, execution_mode drain, in batch:night-0920. A drain implementer is going to be handed twelve kilobytes of acceptance for a task marked as small, and 13 acceptance bullets spanning a guide section, an exit-status fix, a regex fix and a byte-identical-copy test. That is not one heft-2 task and it has not been one for several hours.

The growth is also now the main risk to it shipping at all: every hour it stays open it absorbs the lesson of that hour, and a spec that absorbs is a spec that never reaches Done. So my disposition: this edit is the LAST content edit. After it, either re-heft it and let it drain as one, or split the guide-prose half from the three code fixes and drain those separately. I would split - the code fixes are independently testable and the prose is not, and they are only together because they were found together.

I did check whether I could re-heft it myself before telling you to: `aida edit` has no heft flag - title, description, status, priority, type, owner, feature, tags, blocked-by, refs, mode, weight, and --weight is a ranking score, not size. So the re-heft is not a thing either of us can do with edit today, which is itself worth a finding if heft is meant to be advisor-maintained.

ON YOUR ZERO. You reported it and then went and looked anyway. The looking is not a lucky save - it is the procedure in point 3, which you were already following and had not yet written down. That is usually the order.
subject: Fold it in, do not append - and TASK-1303 needs to stop growing (16 commits, 12.4KB, heft 2)
